items.text: 2/3 The FEHBP is widely considered the gold standard when it comes to affordable healthcare, yet we found that federal workers were being overcharged for drugs so PBMs could pocket the difference in price.

I’m proud to join my friend and colleague @RepMarkGreen to cosponsor this legislation to provide additional healthcare and benefits to K2 veterans. 

As evidenced by our two year investigation, thousands of service members that were deployed to Karshi-Khanabad Air Base in Uzbekistan after September 11th were exposed to multiple toxic hazards and chemicals, including dangerous petrochemicals and burn pits. 

These veterans continue to battle debilitating health conditions, including unusual advanced-stage cancers, and yet the VA refuses to fully acknowledge the link between their service at K2 and their illness. 

We must make every effort to ensure that K2 Veterans and their families receive full healthcare and disability benefits that are reflective of their service and sacrifice to our nation.

This week, the Oversight Committee held a hearing to examine preparations for the next Decennial Census - which the federal government will use to allocate trillions of dollars in federal funding for veterans’ services, healthcare, affordable housing, transportation and infrastructure, and other critical programs.  
 
I urged Census Bureau Director Robert Santos to work more closely with our dedicated Secretary of State Bill Galvin, state and local officials, and community leaders to ensure that we are counting every resident and fully engaging every community in Massachusetts in completing the 2030 Decennial Census.

Great to have met with the Leadership of the American Federation of Government Employees, Local 221. AFGE Local 221 represents our VA Healthcare professionals at the Brockton, West Roxbury, and Jamaica Plain locations.

I strongly condemn the Trump Administration’s attacks against these Doctors and Nurses who provide critical care to our veterans.

As a Member of the @OversightDems Committee and former President of Ironworkers Local 7, I will continue to stand in solidarity with @AFGENational and over 30 other labor organizations that tirelessly advocate for fair wages, safe working conditions, and quality healthcare for federal workers.

Over the last two weeks, President Trump and Elon Musk have arbitrarily fired nearly 3,000 federal employees at the Veterans Administration—including healthcare workers, employees who process benefits claims, and workers who staff the Veterans Crisis Suicide Line to provide mental health support to veterans and their families in crisis.  
 
The Trump Administration carried out these layoffs without regard for the recent audit by the VA Inspector General reporting nearly 3,000 severe staffing shortages for nurses, medical officers, and other frontline healthcare workers at VA healthcare facilities nationwide.  
 
The Veterans Benefits Administration also recently reported a backlog of more than 250,000 disability claims and an average processing time of three to four months.  
 
I asked GAO Comptroller General Gene Dodaro, the chief government watchdog, how these firings will impact care for our Nation’s veterans and their families.

For 60 years,  Medicare and Medicaid have been a lifeline for seniors, families, veterans, and people with disabilities.

Recently, House Republicans voted to slash this lifeline for more than 15 million Americans.

We should be strengthening Medicare and Medicaid, not ripping care away.

I will continue to fight alongside my fellow Democratic colleagues to protect Medicare and Medicaid and reverse these devastating cuts.

We must remember that veterans' healthcare and other benefits are different. When our sons and daughters put on the uniform to serve our country, we make a promise to that veteran that if they return from service with the scars of war – visible or invisible – we will care for them and their families.

Had a great coffee hour yesterday at the Castle Cove Co-op in South Boston to talk with residents about my role in Congress and the challenges we are facing in Washington. We discussed the impact that harmful budget cuts to Medicare and Medicaid would have on seniors and working families, the potential government shutdown and what it would mean for programs like Social Security, and the collapse of Steward Health and its effects on patients and providers. Thank you to Amy Matturro, Tom “Shaper” Nee, Mary Ronca, Alice O'Connor, Bill Ferguson and all the residents for organizing this important conversation and for their kindness and hospitality.

Sincere thanks to Moderator Bob Mullen for allowing me the courtesy of addressing Town Meeting regarding the ongoing government shutdown, my continued opposition to Medicaid cuts and federal layoffs, and the assistance that our Congressional Offices in Brockton, Quincy and Boston can provide to families and veterans in need.

This #VeteransDay, we thank our Nation’s veterans for their sacrifice, service and their example. 

Let us continue to honor our veterans by ensuring that every veteran receives the excellent healthcare and benefits that they have earned by their courageous service to our Nation. 

That is the best way to say - “We thank you for your service!”

Today, I will be voting NO on the Republican Budget bill which would eliminate tax subsidies that working families depend on to afford healthcare and it fails to prevent $1 trillion cuts to Medicaid and Medicare that fund our local Hospitals, Community Health Centers, and Nursing Homes.
